title: THE FOUR OLDS audio play — a12_promotion

lines.sfx: A ventilation fan hums over a long windowless conference room, and a laptop clicks under someone's hands at the head of the table.
Director Holloway, fifties, keeps on down a column on his laptop, and the keys don't stop when the door opens.
Pell comes in, takes the one open chair halfway down, and sets a little espresso cup on the table without a sound.

lines.text: (reading) We're putting the whole Unity Day artifact side under one office. One name on it. Somebody who closes a thing out without leaving a mess behind him.

lines.sfx: Holloway taps the laptop to the next page without looking up.

lines.text: That Nebraska recovery last month. Clean. No press, no lawsuit. Eleven years of that, Pell. This program wants exactly that kind of hand on it.

lines.sfx: Down both sides of the table chairs creak, and somebody flips a page on a desk calendar.

lines.text: Special Administrator, Lunar Heritage Recovery. It's yours. Press'll want you out front on it, and you'll sign off on the Unity Day cargo yourself.

lines.sfx: A leather portfolio slides down the table and stops in front of Pell.
Two seats down, Marsh, forties, already has her phone calendar open.

lines.text: (to Marsh) Marsh. Your office want a piece of the roll—
We're slammed clean through the quarter. Wish we could.

lines.sfx: Pell lays both hands flat on the portfolio.

lines.text: I have to say, thank you. Over on the continent they'd never leave a thing like this to a committee. You give it one owner and it quits drifting. They figured that out a long time ago over there.
(not looking up) Good. Legal's got your paper outside. I've got Denver in five.

lines.sfx: Holloway snaps the laptop shut, chairs slide back all down the table, and the wall screen clicks to the next agenda.

lines.text: You won't have to check up on me, Director. I won't let the Accord down.

lines.sfx: Nobody answers him, and a staffer by the door already has it open.
Out in the carpeted corridor Pell's footsteps slow and stop at a lit trophy case.
He shifts the portfolio to one arm, squares his lanyard, and it clinks once against the glass.
He takes the portfolio back up in both hands, and his footsteps go on down the corridor.
